intro: If you have set up a trust, or you are a trustee of one, you may be searching for trust registration near me because HMRC's Trust Registration Service requires most UK express trusts to be registered and kept up to date. This is a job for a tax adviser who deals with trust registration, and we can introduce you to one in the UK who will quote you directly. The quote is on application, so you can see the cost before deciding.
need_heading: What people searching for trust registration usually need
need_lead: Most enquiries come from trustees who need the trust registered correctly and on time, and who want someone local to handle it.
needs: You have just created a trust and need to know whether it must be registered on HMRC's Trust Registration Service and by when.
You are a trustee of an existing trust that has never been registered and you are worried about deadlines and possible penalties.
The details of a trust have changed, such as the trustees or beneficiaries, and the register needs updating.
You are dealing with a non-UK trust and are unsure whether it falls within the registration rules.
You would rather have a local tax adviser handle the registration and keep the trust's record up to date for you.
context_heading: What to understand about trust registration
context: HMRC's Trust Registration Service is the register on which most UK express trusts, and some non-UK trusts, must be recorded. Deadlines apply after a trust is created, and the register must be kept up to date as things change. Penalties can apply for late registration, so it is worth dealing with it promptly.

"Tax adviser" is not a protected title in the UK. The Chartered Institute of Taxation, for the CTA qualification, and the Association of Taxation Technicians are the main specialist bodies, and many accountants and solicitors also advise on tax. Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, so it is reasonable to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are looking for help with trust registration near you and whether you are a trustee or acting for one.
Describe the type of trust, such as whether it is a UK express trust or a non-UK trust.
Say whether the trust is new or already exists and whether it has been registered before.
Mention any changes that need updating on the register, such as trustees or beneficiaries.
Give your location so we can introduce you to a suitable UK professional near you.
Say whether you want help with the registration only or ongoing help keeping the record up to date.
questions: Does this trust need to be registered on HMRC's Trust Registration Service?
What is the deadline for registering this trust, and what happens if it is missed?
What information will you need from me to complete the registration?
How will changes to the trust be updated on the register, and who is responsible for that?
What are your qualifications and are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance, and how will you quote for this work?

faqs.q: Does every trust need to be registered?
faqs.a: No. Most UK express trusts must be registered on HMRC's Trust Registration Service, and some non-UK trusts must be too, but not every trust is caught. A tax adviser can tell you whether your particular trust needs registering.

faqs.q: What happens if a trust is registered late?
faqs.a: Penalties can apply for late registration, so it is better to deal with it promptly. A tax adviser can explain the position for your trust and help you put things right.

faqs.q: Do I need to update the register after it is set up?
faqs.a: Yes. The register must be kept up to date, so changes such as new trustees or beneficiaries need to be recorded. A tax adviser can handle this for you or show you how it works.

faqs.q: Can you help with a non-UK trust?
faqs.a: Some non-UK trusts must be registered on HMRC's Trust Registration Service. Tell us about the trust when you enquire and we can introduce you to a UK tax adviser who deals with this.
